Cannabis can help treat opioid addiction, study shows
So, literally the exact opposite of a gateway drug?
People against cannabis usually bring the argument that it is only a stepping stone to harder drugs (i.e if you use Cannabis you'll eventually use Meth).

Misleading title. It doesn't treat the addiction exactly. It helps treat withdrawal symptoms so that the patient is more comfortable going through the detox process, much like how marijuana is used to treat the uncomfortable side effects cancer patients experience when they go through chemo. The article doesn't say, but implies that the use of marijuana for the addict ceases after detox. Otherwise you're just substituting drugs and they'll be back to opiates inside of a week.

Edit: also, real addiction recovery doesn't happen with the use of drugs/pharmaceuticals. The drug use is just a symptom of the disease. It's really a disease of the mind and you have to relearn the way you think, feel, and live.

Source: am addict.

But yeah, I'm sure cannabis will soothe people while they are detoxing, but as far as maintenance for addiction that's pretty ridiculous. When you're addicted to one drug, it's pretty much a guarantee you're addicted to EVERYTHING else. The gene has been turned on. You might start out with weed, but if you're choice of drug is heroin you'll be back to it in no time.

And like I said before, the drug use is just a symptom of addiction. Addiction is a disease of the mind that presents itself through obsessive compulsions, usually things that either numb you emotionally or give you a rush or sense of euphoria. Now that can range from dope, to sex, to gambling, to cars, skydiving, exercise, affection - pretty much anything. It depends on how it effects your life and if it dominates it or is destructive.

An IP ban based on other accounts is a reasonable ban. The real issues with this is that IP address for consumer networks are typically dynamic. Which could easily lead to users being banned during an IP change. Also, for shared IPs etc etc. IP banning really should only be used in the most extreme situations.

Theoretically, If a ship somehow had negative mass, could it surpass the speed of light?

Short answer: First of all, negative mass is forbidden by relativity, so it can not exist in our universe. Secondly, even if particles with negative mass somehow existed, they would still obey relativity, so no, they could not surpass the speed of light.

Long answer: you already linked it: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Negative_mass

No, it's rest mass needs to be imaginary (as in complex numbers). You could model the ship as a tachyon and use the same calculation for mass.
